idea.body: Multiplying decimals means multiplying the digits as if there were no decimal point, then counting decimal digits to place the point in the answer. Count how many decimal digits the two numbers have together, then put the point that many digits in from the right of the product. Dividing by a decimal number first turns it into a whole number, by moving its decimal point. The number being divided moves its point the same number of places. Cutting 0.3 meters of wire for 0.4 of a job: 3 times 4 is 12, and two decimal digits together makes it 0.12 meters.

figure.alt: A grid of 10 rows and 10 columns, with a 3 by 4 rectangle of 12 squares shaded, showing 0.3 times 0.4 equals 0.12.

workedExample.prompt: A workshop cuts 2.4 meters of wire per bracket. How much wire does 3 brackets need?
steps: Multiply as if 2.4 were a whole number: 24 times 3 is 72.
2.4 has one decimal digit, so the answer needs one decimal digit too.
Counting one place in from the right of 72 gives 7.2.
Three brackets need 7.2 meters of wire.

ways.name: Multiply then place the point
ways.when: Use this for any decimal multiplication, no matter how many decimal digits each number has.
steps: Multiply the digits as if there were no decimal points at all.
Count how many decimal digits the two numbers have altogether.
Place the decimal point that many digits in from the right of the product.
ways.trap: Counting decimal digits in the answer's own length instead of adding up the original numbers' decimal digits.

ways.name: Move both decimal points together
ways.when: Use this when dividing by a number that has a decimal point.
steps: Count how many places to move the divisor's decimal point to make it a whole number.
Move the number being divided by that same number of places.
Divide as usual, now with a whole number divisor.
ways.trap: Moving the two decimal points by a different number of places instead of matching them exactly.

ways.name: Break into friendly parts
ways.when: Use this when one of the decimal numbers splits neatly into easier pieces.
steps: Split one number into a whole part and a decimal part.
Multiply each part by the other number separately.
ways.trap: Multiplying only the whole part by the other number and forgetting the decimal part.

ways.name: Double and double again
ways.when: Use this when the whole number you are multiplying by is a power of 2, like 2, 4 or 8.
steps: Double the decimal number once for each time you multiply by 2.
Multiply by 4 by doubling twice; multiply by 8 by doubling three times.
The last double is your answer.
ways.trap: Doubling one too many or too few times and landing on the wrong power of 2.

bank.prompt: A 3D printer uses a fixed length of filament for each identical part it prints, in meters. Each part uses 3.2 m. What is the total for 2 parts, in meters?
explanation: Multiply as if 3.2 were a whole number: 32 times 2.
3.2 has 1 decimal digit, so the product needs the same number of decimal digits.
3.2 times 2 is 6.4.
bank.useAgain: when you multiply two numbers that both have digits after the decimal point.
hints: Multiply the two numbers as if neither had a decimal point at all.
Count the total number of decimal digits in both numbers you multiplied. Put the point that many places from the right in the product.
bank.socraticHint: Does multiplying two numbers smaller than one ever give a product bigger than either of them?
